problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=xyz-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz),$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(1,0,\pi ).$
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz-\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz)-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)) \\  & =yz\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x)-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)) \\  & =yz\cdot 1-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)) \\  & =yz-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz))\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}yz-\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xz)) & =yz-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(xz) \\  & =yz-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz)\cdot (z) \\  & =yz-z\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz) \\  & =z(y-\operatorname{cos}⁡(xz))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,0,\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(1,0,\pi )} & =\pi (0-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1\cdot \pi )) \\  & =\pi (0-(-1)) \\  & =\pi \end{aligned}
$$
